Vanguard

/VAN-gard/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Vanguard means the foremost or leading position in a movement, field, or advancing group.

The small Antwerp studio stood in the vanguard of sustainable fashion years before the big houses followed.

Worked Example

In 2009, while major automakers were still mocking battery power, a scrappy motorcycle shop in Oregon began converting dirt bikes to electric drive. They published their designs freely, raced their prototypes against gasoline machines, and lost — then improved and raced again. Within a decade, three of their engineers had been hired away to lead programs at the very companies that once laughed. Historians of the industry now describe that little shop as the vanguard of the electric-motorcycle movement: the ones out front before there was even a road.

The shop leads the movement years before anyone else follows — out front, taking the risks first — which is exactly the position the vanguard occupies.

How Vanguard Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

forefront

forefront: the leading edge or position

Antonyms

stragglers

stragglers: those trailing behind

How Strong Is It? — front → vanguard → spearhead

front vs. vanguard

front vs. vanguard: Front is the plain, weaker word — anything can be at the front of a line; the vanguard is the leading edge of an advancing movement, out ahead by choice and risk.

spearhead vs. vanguard

spearhead vs. vanguard: Spearhead is sharper and stronger than vanguard: it names the single point driving the advance, while the vanguard is the whole leading body.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of vanguard.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — van

Root — van: front, before (French avant)

Root — guard

Root — guard: to guard, to watch (French garde)

Put it together

Put it together: Vanguard is French avant-garde squeezed into English: avant (before) plus garde (guard) — the detachment that marched ahead of a medieval army, first into danger. English clipped avant to van- and kept the meaning: whoever is out front, taking the first risks of an advance. The garde root still stands watch in guard and guardian, and the full French original survives in English as avant-garde, the label for artists ahead of their time.

Use the root in a new word: avant-garde

Use the root in a new word: avant-garde: Critics called the composer avant-garde decades before audiences caught up — avant-garde is the unshortened French original of vanguard, literally the 'fore-guard' marching ahead of the army.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal; journalism and history ('in the vanguard of...')

Vanguard names the leading PEOPLE or GROUP of a movement — researchers, artists, troops — usually in the phrase 'in the vanguard of.' For a topic or issue that has merely become prominent ('at the forefront of the agenda'), forefront is the idiomatic choice, not vanguard.
